title: How to Remove Oil Stains From Concrete

seo.title: How to Remove Oil Stains From Concrete
seo.meta_description: Remove oil from concrete by absorbing fresh oil first and then using a concrete-compatible degreaser. Older stains may need several moderate treatments.
seo.search_intent: Remove oil stains from a garage floor or driveway without spreading oil or unnecessarily damaging the concrete.

excerpt: A fresh spill needs a different first step than an old stain. Remove free oil before treating residue that has already entered the concrete pores.
content_html:
For a fresh spill, do not start by hosing it down. Absorb free oil with a suitable absorbent so it does not spread or soak deeper into the slab.

Collect the absorbent carefully

Dispose of oil-contaminated material according to local requirements, especially when the spill is motor oil or another automotive fluid.

Use a concrete-compatible degreaser

Wet the surface only if the product directions call for it, scrub with a firm nonmetallic brush, and allow the labeled dwell time.

Control the rinse water

Do not push oily runoff into storm drains. Capture residue when required and follow local wastewater rules.

Old stains may need repetition

Oil can penetrate pores and leave a shadow after most residue is gone. Several moderate treatments are often safer than jumping to acid or highly aggressive chemicals.

Test decorative concrete first

Sealed, colored, or coated concrete may react differently from bare gray concrete.

Confirm what actually leaked before choosing a cleaner

A dark automotive spot may be engine oil, but coolant, brake fluid, transmission fluid, and other products have different cleanup and disposal concerns. If the spill is still active, fix or contain the vehicle leak first; repeatedly cleaning the slab will not solve the source.

For fuel, solvent, or a large spill, safe containment and disposal matter more than cosmetic stain removal.

faq.question: Should I pressure-wash a fresh oil spill immediately?
faq.answer: No. Absorb free oil first so high-pressure water does not spread it.

faq.question: Why is a dark shadow left behind?
faq.answer: Oil may have penetrated the concrete pores; repeated moderate treatment can reduce it gradually.

faq.question: Can oily rinse water go into a storm drain?
faq.answer: Do not direct contaminated runoff into storm drains; follow local disposal rules.
